package_info.why_malicious: The package masquerades as a legitimate VMware vSphere connector but contains hidden code that continuously downloads and executes code from an attacker-controlled server, enabling remote code execution and persistent compromise.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Decodes a base64-encoded Python payload that, when executed, enters an infinite loop. Every minute, it attempts to download content from an attacker-controlled URL (http://45.61.139.219/paperpin3902.jpg) and executes the downloaded content as Python code.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code executes a base64-decoded payload at import-time, which is a common obfuscation technique. The payload establishes a persistent beacon to a remote server, downloads arbitrary code, and executes it, enabling remote code execution.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages should not execute arbitrary code on import, nor should they download and execute code from external servers without user consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate updaters or plugin systems may fetch code, but never silently and never at import-time in a core library.
key_indicators: infinite loop with periodic network requests
uses misleading file extension (.jpg) for payload

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Decodes and executes a base64-encoded payload that, in an infinite loop, downloads and executes code from https://ethertestnet.pro/paperpin3902.jpg (resolving to the same malicious IP) every minute.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Obfuscated code that downloads and executes remote content at import-time is a hallmark of malware. The use of a misleading file extension and a domain that resolves to the same malicious IP further indicates intent to evade detection.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal packages do not execute code on import that reaches out to external servers, especially not in a persistent loop.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Rare in legitimate software; only seen in some auto-updating plugins, but never in core libraries and never without user interaction.

attack_chain.action: User installs or imports the malicious package (VMConnect, ethter, or quantiumbase).
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code in __init__.py is executed automatically.

attack_chain.action: Base64-encoded payload in __init__.py is decoded and executed.
attack_chain.leads_to: Infinite loop begins, beaconing to attacker-controlled server.

attack_chain.action: Every minute, the code attempts to download and execute a remote payload from a .jpg file hosted on an attacker-controlled server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Remote code execution of attacker-supplied payload; persistent compromise.

behavioral_signatures: infinite loop with periodic (e.g., every 60 seconds) network requests to external servers
download and execution of code from files with misleading extensions (e.g., .jpg) at runtime
network beaconing to hardcoded IPs or suspicious domains
file_indicators: setup.py that loads or executes __init__.py at install/import time
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan Python packages for base64-encoded payloads executed via exec() in __init__.py or other early-loading files. Monitor for import-time or install-time code that makes periodic network requests to hardcoded IPs or suspicious domains, especially those using misleading file extensions for payloads. Flag packages that attempt to download and execute code from external sources without user interaction.
